They offer up as sweet fragrance to God and Father our Lord Jesus the Christ, first indeed as having him through the Spirit both dwelling and having been inhabited, second that, proclaiming everywhere and carrying about the word upon him, just as a kind of most pleasant of incenses, they were bringing to God the zeal with this; thirdly in a way, that also having become conformed to him, through equal sufferings they were perfected. They say that they are full of the fragrance of Christ among the being saved and among the being destroyed, to those indeed an odor from death unto death, to those however an odor from life unto life, it was following to observe. Surely it should be understood toward us appropriately, according to the proper aim for contemplations, the believing ones and those following the faith, and those on the one hand not yet having known God by nature and truly, but having rather worshipped the creation instead of the Creator. These, not approaching the word of the divine proclamation, but rather mocking and having deemed the mystery of Christ to be foolishness, receive 'the odor of the knowledge' of the Father, from death unto death; for being in death, through that ignorance and hardness dwelling in them, they might fall by only once and a second death; those indeed having been brought by means of the legal instruction toward the beginnings of the knowledge of God, having become somewhat in life, if they would but believe, they would receive the odor of the knowledge of the Father from life unto life.

For he says at some time Christ to the Father and God in the heavens: 'And this is eternal life, that they may know you the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ.' But who would be capable regarding these things, he says? And most fittingly: For truly difficult is that which anyone might be able to speak rightly and without error the mystery of Christ, which certain divine disciples were, and correcting the wanderings of the heterodox, to whom it is custom and through greater zeal has been set to love to always make the like of usurping the Word of God, and the return of the faith having been crushed by deceit and falsehood: For it is not possible among them to find the truth unalloyed as also unborrowed; But the divine mystagogues speaking in Spirit, as from sincerity before God all things they do and say. You are our letter, written in our hearts. We do not ask for testimony through words, for you, the disciples and faithful of Christ, approving in these very things, have crowned us your teachers and shown us to be acceptable. Therefore our letter you are, written in our hearts, that is, always and throughout, in the memory lying with us: For we are always being glorified, he says, in you. Not on stone tablets, but on tablets of the heart of flesh. And he seals also with prophetic testimony: 'Not on stone tablets, but on tablets of the heart of flesh.'

pass_b_english: They offer up as a sweet fragrance to God and Father our Lord Jesus Christ. First, they do this because they possess Him through the Spirit, who both dwells in them and has made a home within them. Second, because they proclaim and carry the Word upon them everywhere, they bring to God a zeal that is like one of the most pleasant of incenses.
Thirdly, they are perfected through equal sufferings, having become conformed to Him.

It is observed that they are full of the fragrance of Christ, both among those being saved and among those being destroyed; for some, it is an odor from death unto death, while for others, it is an odor from life unto life.

Surely, it is appropriate for us to understand the situation of those among us—both the believers and those who pursue the faith, and those who have not yet known God truly or by nature but have instead worshipped the creation rather than the Creator—according to the proper aim of spiritual contemplation.

These latter, not approaching the Word of the divine proclamation but rather mocking it and regarding the mystery of Christ as foolishness, receive 'the odor of the knowledge' of the Father, leading from death unto death.
For being in a state of death, through the ignorance and hardness dwelling within them, they might fall by the first and the second death.

Those who have been brought by means of legal instruction toward the beginnings of the knowledge of God have indeed attained a kind of life; yet, if they would only believe, they would receive the odor of the knowledge of the Father from life unto life.

For he says that Christ at some time spoke to the Father and God in the heavens: "And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ" (John 17:3). But he asks, who could be capable of such things? And most fittingly so.

It is truly difficult for anyone to be able to speak the mystery of Christ rightly and without error. Certain divine disciples were such, correcting the wanderings of those who think differently; yet it is their custom, through a great zeal, to love to always usurp the Word of God, having always crushed the return of the faith through deceit and falsehood.
For it is not possible for them to find the truth unalloyed or unborrowed.
But the divine mystagogues, speaking in the Spirit, do and say all things with sincerity before God.
You are our letter, written upon our hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3).

We do not ask for testimony through words; for you, the disciples and faithful of Christ, by approving in these very matters, have crowned us your teachers and shown us to be acceptable (2 Corinthians 3:2).
Therefore, you are our letter, written in our hearts—that is, always and throughout, held in the memory that lies with us.
For he says, we are always being glorified in you.
Not on stone tablets, but on tablets of the heart of flesh (Jeremiah 31:33).
And he seals this also with prophetic testimony: "Not on stone tablets, but on tablets of the heart of flesh."

For he says that God once spoke through the voice of a prophet, saying, 'Behold, the days are coming,' says the Lord, 'and I will make a new covenant for the house of Israel and for the house of Judah, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide in my covenant; yet I cared for them,' says the Lord.

I will put my laws into their mind, and upon their hearts I will write them, for this is the covenant that I will make for the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord. For of old, the lawgiver Moses received the law on stone tablets, as it has been written.
We say that this has become a riddle of the hardness of heart of the Jews.
For it is rather unacceptable to their own minds to reject the law, and it is like something briefly and scarcely engraved in stones, except...
